oauthNotes: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect through the Microsoft identity platform. Apps are registered in Microsoft Entra ID and call Microsoft Graph.

composio.note: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Outlook, so development can start without registering your own. A custom OAuth app is needed for your own branding on the consent screen, dedicated quota, or scopes beyond Composio's defaults.

summary: Registering an app in Microsoft Entra ID is immediate and has no review. For a multitenant app, the practical requirement is publisher verification: without it, users in other organisations are often unable to consent. Verification is free and takes minutes once a verified Microsoft partner account exists.

verdict.headline: Testing is available within minutes. Production access for users in other organisations requires publisher verification, which completes in minutes once a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account and a custom domain are in place.
verdict.biggestRisk: Where risk-based step-up consent is enabled, users cannot consent to a multitenant app from an unverified publisher, and many organisations require administrator consent regardless.

paths.name: Multitenant app for other organisations
paths.whenThisApplies: Users in any Microsoft Entra tenant, and optionally personal Microsoft accounts, connect their mailbox. This is the usual case for a SaaS agent.

timeToFirstLogin.basis: App registration and a test sign-in in your own tenant.

activeEffort.basis: Estimate. Partner account enrolment, domain verification and configuration. No direct source.

waitTime.basis: Estimate. Microsoft states that verification completes in minutes once the prerequisites are met. The time to verify a new partner account is not stated in the sources read.

timeToProduction.basis: Estimate. Depends on whether a verified partner account already exists.

paths.cost: No charge for publisher verification. An Azure account with an active subscription is listed as a prerequisite for registration.

steps.title: Use a work or school account in an Entra tenant
steps.detail: Register the app with a Microsoft Entra work or school account. Apps registered with a personal Microsoft account cannot be publisher verified.

steps.title: Register the application
steps.detail: In the Microsoft Entra admin centre, open App registrations and select New registration. Choose a multitenant account type.
gotchas: The application cannot be moved between tenants after creation.

steps.title: Add the redirect URI and a client secret
steps.detail: Add a Web platform redirect URI and create a client secret. Add both to a Composio auth config.

steps.title: Select delegated permissions
steps.detail: The agent proposes the narrowest Microsoft Graph delegated permissions. High-privilege permissions require administrator consent.

steps.title: Enrol in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program
steps.detail: Create or use the organisation's partner global account and complete its verification.
gotchas: The partner account's email domain must match the app's publisher domain or a DNS-verified custom domain.
The publisher domain cannot be an onmicrosoft.com domain.

steps.title: Microsoft verifies the partner account
steps.detail: Verification of a new partner account is handled by Microsoft Partner Center.

estTime.basis: Estimate. Not stated in the sources read.

steps.title: Mark the app as publisher verified
steps.detail: Associate the verified Partner ID with the app registration, signed in with multifactor authentication.

estTime.basis: Microsoft: verified in minutes once requirements are met.

paths.name: Single-tenant app for your own organisation
paths.whenThisApplies: Only users in your own Microsoft Entra tenant use the app.

waitTime.basis: No provider review on this path.

timeToProduction.basis: No verification is needed inside your own tenant.

steps.title: Register a single-tenant application
steps.detail: Microsoft recommends the single-tenant option for most applications.

steps.title: Grant administrator consent
steps.detail: An administrator grants consent once for the organisation.

requirements.item: Microsoft Entra tenant with a work or school account
requirements.detail: The registering account needs at least the Application Developer role.

requirements.item: Verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account
requirements.detail: It must be the organisation's partner global account.
Set as the app's publisher domain. An onmicrosoft.com domain is not accepted.
Required for the user who initiates verification.

requirements.item: Administrator roles in Entra ID and Partner Center
requirements.detail: Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator, and CPP Partner Admin or Account Admin.

nuances.title: Unverified publishers are blocked from user consent
nuances.detail: Where risk-based step-up consent is enabled, users cannot consent to most multitenant apps registered after 8 November 2020 that are not publisher verified and request more than basic sign-in.

nuances.title: Administrators may need to consent
nuances.detail: Application permissions and many high-privilege delegated permissions can be granted only by an administrator.

nuances.title: Refresh tokens last 90 days
nuances.detail: The default lifetime is 90 days, or 24 hours for single-page applications. Each use returns a replacement token.

nuances.title: Refresh tokens can be revoked at any time
nuances.detail: The sign-in service can revoke tokens before expiry, for example after an administrator action. The agent must handle re-authentication.

nuances.title: Publisher verification is free
nuances.detail: Microsoft does not charge for it and no licence is required.

blockers.symptom: Users see an unverified publisher warning and cannot consent
blockers.cause: The app is multitenant and not publisher verified.
blockers.fix: Complete publisher verification. Until then, ask a tenant administrator to grant consent.

blockers.cause: The requested permissions are high privilege, or the tenant restricts user consent.
blockers.fix: Reduce the requested permissions, or provide the customer's administrator with an admin consent link.

blockers.cause: The partner account's email domain does not match the publisher domain, or the publisher domain is an onmicrosoft.com domain.
blockers.fix: Add and DNS-verify a custom domain in the tenant and set it as the publisher domain.

handoffKit.title: Register the app with Azure CLI
handoffKit.content:
az ad app create \
  --display-name "<Your product name>" \
  --sign-in-audience AzureADandPersonalMicrosoftAccount \
  --web-redirect-uris https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback

# Drafted from the Azure CLI reference, not executed. Confirm the flags with: az ad app create --help

handoffKit.title: App registration values
handoffKit.content:
Name: <Your product name>
Supported account types: Any Entra ID tenant + personal Microsoft accounts (or Multiple Entra ID tenants for work accounts only)
Redirect URI (Web): https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback
Publisher domain: <yourdomain> (custom, DNS verified)

handoffKit.title: Permission selection
handoffKit.content:
Request delegated permissions only, and the narrowest that work.
Read mail: Mail.Read. Send mail: Mail.Send. Read and write mail: Mail.ReadWrite.
Calendar: Calendars.Read or Calendars.ReadWrite.
Include offline_access to receive refresh tokens.
Permission names are from the Microsoft Graph reference and were not re-verified in this research.

handoffKit.title: Connect the OAuth app to Composio
handoffKit.content:
1. In the Composio dashboard, open Auth Configs and create one for Outlook using OAuth2 with your own developer credentials.
2. Enter the client ID and client secret. Set the redirect URI to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback
3. Pass the auth config ID (ac_...) in your session's authConfigs, keyed by toolkit. Creating the auth config alone does not apply it.
Reference: https://docs.composio.dev/docs/authentication/custom-app-vs-managed-app
